answer: No -- ZERO IS THE WIRE ENCODING OF ONE, and writing the literal one broke admission for all three DeepSeek-V4-Flash cells.
how_a_gate_missed_it: the gate that passed the change was a walk with verify=False.  The A18 encoding is checked by the ABI verifier, not by execution, so the only gate that could see it was one that admits.  A token walk that skips admission cannot gate a descriptor-encoding change.

at_head_with_the_numerator_written_as_on.consequence: none of the three V4-Flash cells can execute
at_head_with_the_numerator_written_as_on.how: tools/run_accelerator_tokens.py on TA-DS-CHAT-1-P32, which admits mandatorily and has no override

at_the_commit_before_the_a18_change.note: that digest is the deployment_digest_binding recorded in the CLOSED token artifact, so the pre-change state is the verified one

question: was 'an A18 numerator of exactly ONE was silently encoded as zero' a defect?

suite_gate.method: tests/compiler and tests/abi3 run twice -- once in a worktree at HEAD, once on this change -- and the two failing-node SETS compared.  A bare count is not a gate here: 123 nodes fail at HEAD for reasons this change does not touch (source-currency drift across bound artifacts), so only the set difference says anything.
suite_gate.reading: twelve nodes are repaired and none regress.  Every repaired node is a DeepSeek-V4-Flash or array admission test, which is exactly the blast radius the 116-view admission failure predicted.

what_survives_from_the_attempt: the JOINT test.  All three extent fields are zeroed only for A13's own identity -- 1 * value / 1 + 0 -- so a view needing no A18 stays byte-identical to the pre-amendment form and a view whose only A18 content is a bias keeps that bias.

what_the_abi_says.resolver: runtime/sim/memory.py resolves the field as max(int(payload['extent_numerator']), 1), so zero on the wire IS one
what_the_abi_says.verifier: amendment A18 encodes a numerator of one as zero, so a declared one is a value the wire format does not assign; write zero

why_the_original_reading_was_wrong: I read a zero numerator as 'no extent declared' and concluded that zeroing a numerator of one deleted a symbolic term while leaving its bias behind.  The bias is written independently either way, so nothing was ever dropped; and the resolver reads zero back as one, so the term was never deleted.
